html:
Valletta, the capital of Malta, was founded on 28 March 1566 by the Grand Master Jean de la Valette, after the Great Siege. It was one of the first planned cities of early modern Europe.

The pope's military engineer Francesco Laparelli laid out a grid of straight streets on a rocky peninsula between two harbours, ringed with bastions. The Knights built their palaces, their hospital and the Co-Cathedral of St John there. Caravaggio painted for the order in Valletta.

Under British rule from 1800 the Grand Harbour was the base of the Mediterranean fleet. The city was heavily bombed in the siege of the Second World War. The whole city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
sum: Valletta, the capital of Malta, was founded on 28 March 1566 by the Grand Master Jean de la Valette, after the Great Siege. It was one of the first planned cities of early modern Europe.
